label: conj:explicit-central-idempotent
title: The four Murphy–Lagrange cross-checks for $e_\lambda$ follow from Lagrange interpolation in commuting variables
html:
Conjecture. The four Murphy–Lagrange cross-checks for e_\lambda follow from Lagrange interpolation in commuting variables

Conjecture. Let H_n(q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra over a commutative ring R at generic q, and let

  e_\lambda \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} \; \prod_{k=1}^{n} \; \prod_{\substack{\square \in \lambda \\ \square \neq T(k)}} \frac{J_k - c(\square; q)}{c(T(k); q) - c(\square; q)}

be the Murphy–Lagrange element attached to a partition \lambda \vdash n, built from the Jucys–Murphy elements J_1, \ldots, J_n and the q-contents c(\square; q) = q^{2(j-i)} of the boxes of \lambda. Then the four cross-checks

  1. sum-to-identity — \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} e_\lambda = 1;
  2. orthogonality — e_\lambda e_\mu = \delta_{\lambda\mu} \, e_\lambda, in particular idempotency e_\lambda^2 = e_\lambda;
  3. self-adjointness — \star(e_\lambda) = e_\lambda for self-conjugate \lambda = \lambda';
  4. bar-pairing — \star(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda'} for a chiral pair \lambda \neq \lambda'

all follow from Lagrange interpolation in the commuting variables J_1, \ldots, J_n.

Why this is stated separately

The cross-checks are what makes e_\lambda the central primitive idempotent rather than merely an element of Z(H_n(q)), and they are the sole unproved input to prop:explicit-central-idempotent. That proposition is proved in Lean conditionally on them, with the class carrying them as an explicit instance hypothesis. Naming the conjecture as its own block is what lets the proposition's uses[] record the dependency, so the conditional cone is auditable from the manifest and not only from the Lean signature.

Status

Open. The carrier is the class QOU.BraidKnot.ExplicitCentralIdempotent.ExplicitCentralIdempotentConjecture, whose field states cross-check 2 — the one downstream Lean consumes — quantified over every partition of every n, so it is a claim about the whole construction and not about one \lambda. No instance of the class exists anywhere in the corpus, which is the correct representation of an unproved primary conjecture: an instance would assert the statement, not prove it.

The J_k diagonal action that the interpolation argument rests on is itself established — prop:jucys-murphy-central-elements-qou gives pairwise commutation and the eigenvalue J_k \cdot v_T = c_T(k;q) \cdot v_T on the Hoefsmit seminormal basis (prop:hoefsmit-seminormal-form). What is missing is the step from that diagonal action to the four identities, which is the interpolation argument proper.

Scope of the Lean carrier

The class carries the interpolation-theoretic inputs, not the cross-checks themselves: an index type \mathrm{Tab}(\lambda) of standard tableaux, a projector \pi_T for each, and three properties —

  • \pi_T^2 = \pi_T (Lagrange interpolation at a simple joint eigenvalue),
  • \pi_T \pi_{T'} = 0 for T \neq T' (distinct tableaux carry distinct joint eigenvalue tuples),
  • e_\lambda = \sum_T \pi_T.

Cross-check 2 is then derived: e_\lambda^2 = \sum_T \sum_{T'} \pi_T \pi_{T'} = \sum_T \pi_T^2 = \sum_T \pi_T = e_\lambda.

This replaces an earlier encoding that violated AGENTS.md §3b-cond item 5. Until 2026-09-04 the class had a single field whose type was prop:explicit-central-idempotent's conclusion, discharged by a bare projection exact hi.idempotent lam h — so the "conditional theorem" proved nothing modulo the class. Caught by the --item5 mode of scripts/conditional-on-class-hypothesis-audit.ts; the fix was to axiomatise what interpolation actually supplies and let the theorem compose it.

Cross-checks 1, 3 and 4 (sum-to-identity, self-adjointness, bar-pairing) are stated above but are still not encoded — they have no downstream consumer yet. Orthogonality is now encoded, at the projector level, because idempotency needs it. Per §3b-tax no instance of the class exists, which is the correct representation of an unproved primary conjecture.
